headline: AirTrunk, the data-centre operator owned by Blackstone, has postponed a planned Singapore share listing that could raise about $1.5 billion, as AI and tech shares fall.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large AI-infrastructure listing is delayed and a second one has been scrapped, but it rests on two unnamed sources and no new date is set.
importance_line: Investors and lenders weighing data-centre projects get a sign that large AI-infrastructure offerings are harder to sell during a share sell-off, but the delay rests on two unnamed sources, no new date is set, and AirTrunk and Blackstone have not explained it.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by The Straits Times and citing two people with direct knowledge, that AirTrunk, the data-centre operator owned by the investment firm Blackstone, has put off a planned initial public offering of a Singapore real estate investment trust (REIT, a listed fund that owns property) that could raise about $1.5 billion and was expected to be valued at about $15 billion, because of market conditions during a tech and AI share sell-off. AirTrunk, which had planned to launch in September or October, has not set a new date but aims to list by early 2027, one of the sources said, and the report says the delay follows the scrapping of Firmus's planned IPO, a sign of a harder climate for large data-centre and AI-linked listings as investors reassess valuations, borrowing costs and the durability of demand.
notes: Read in full via fulltext; the text is Reuters's (ends REUTERS), carried by The Straits Times. Currency of the dollar figures is not stated in the text.
